scope: Genesis 26–28, all 103 verses. Genesis 1–25 and James remain unchanged.

source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact UTF-8 <verse ...>...</verse> substring, including markup, whitespace, written forms, and any reading notes. No XML reserialization or Hebrew normalization.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive or textual choice. Editorial choices, not automated similarity bins. Independent review pending.

verses.rationale: Keep the distinction between the two famines; place Gerar before the royal identification for a clear destination.
verses.before: Now there was a famine in the land, besides the former famine that had occurred in the days of Abraham. And Isaac went to Abimelech king of the Philistines at Gerar.
verses.after: Another famine came over the land, apart from the earlier famine in Abraham’s time. Isaac went to Gerar, to Abimelech, king of the Philistines.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now there was a famine in the land, besides the former famine that had occurred in the days of Abraham. And Isaac went to Abimelech king of the Philistines at Gerar.

verses.rationale: Identify the recipient at the opening of divine speech; keep the prohibition and the promised direction distinct.
verses.before: And the LORD appeared to him and said, “Do not go down to Egypt. Dwell in the land of which I will tell you.
verses.after: The LORD appeared to Isaac and said, “Do not go down to Egypt. Stay in the land I tell you to live in.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD appeared to him and said, “Do not go down to Egypt. Dwell in the land of which I shall tell you.

verses.rationale: Render gur as residence without native standing; retain all these lands, presence, blessing, and the sworn oath.
verses.before: Sojourn in this land, and I will be with you and bless you, for to you and to your offspring I will give all these lands, and I will establish the oath that I swore to Abraham your father.
verses.after: Live in this land as a stranger, and I will be with you and bless you. I will give all these lands to you and your descendants, and fulfill the oath I swore to your father Abraham.
verses.tsw_comparator: Sojourn in this land, and I will be with you and bless you, for to you and to your offspring I will give all these lands, and I will establish the oath that I swore to Abraham your father.

verses.rationale: Use the same find-blessing rendering as 22:18 for the Hitpael; flag reflexive blessing-by-name as a consequential alternative.
verses.before: I will multiply your offspring like the stars of the heavens and will give to your offspring all these lands. And in your offspring all the nations of the earth will be blessed,
verses.after: I will make your descendants as numerous as the stars of the heavens and give them all these lands. Through your descendants all the nations of the earth will find blessing,
verses.tsw_comparator: I will multiply your offspring like the stars of the heavens and will give to your offspring all these lands. And in your offspring all the nations of the earth shall be blessed,

verses.rationale: Preserve the causal link to Abraham and the layered legal vocabulary rather than compressing everything to obedience.
verses.before: because Abraham obeyed my voice and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.”
verses.after: because Abraham listened to my voice and kept what I entrusted to him: my commands, my statutes, and my instructions.”
verses.tsw_comparator: because Abraham obeyed my voice and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.”

verses.rationale: Render the short wayyiqtol transition directly without an unnecessary inference marker.
verses.before: So Isaac settled in Gerar.
verses.after: Isaac stayed in Gerar.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Isaac settled in Gerar.

verses.rationale: Clarify the transition into Isaac’s fear while retaining the source’s explicit description of Rebekah’s appearance.
verses.before: When the men of the place asked him about his wife, he said, “She is my sister,” for he feared to say, “My wife,” thinking, “The men of the place may kill me because of Rebekah,” because she was beautiful in appearance.
verses.after: When the men there asked about his wife, Isaac said, “She is my sister.” He was afraid to say, “My wife.” “The men here might kill me because of Rebekah,” he thought—she was beautiful.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the men of the place asked him about his wife, he said, “She is my sister,” for he feared to say, “My wife,” thinking, “The men of the place may kill me because of Rebekah,” because she was beautiful in appearance.

verses.rationale: Choose intimate caressing for metsacheq in this husband-wife context; record its laughter/play connection rather than importing it into the English mechanically.
verses.before: When he had been there a long time, Abimelech king of the Philistines looked out through a window and saw Isaac caressing Rebekah his wife.
verses.after: After Isaac had been there a long time, Abimelech, king of the Philistines, looked out a window and saw Isaac caressing his wife Rebekah.
verses.tsw_comparator: When he had been there a long time, Abimelech king of the Philistines looked out through a window and saw Isaac caressing Rebekah his wife.

verses.rationale: Separate the accusation and answer; interpret death in the context of the stated fear of killing in verse 7.
verses.before: Then Abimelech called Isaac and said, “Look, she is your wife! How then could you say, ‘She is my sister’?” Isaac said to him, “Because I thought I might die because of her.”
verses.after: Abimelech summoned Isaac. “She is your wife!” he said. “How could you say, ‘She is my sister’?” Isaac answered, “I thought I might be killed because of her.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Abimelech called Isaac and said, “Behold, she is your wife! How then could you say, ‘She is my sister’?” Isaac said to him, “Because I thought I might die because of her.”

verses.rationale: Retain sexual intercourse, the unrealized risk, and communal guilt without adding an account of consent the verse does not give.
verses.before: Abimelech said, “What is this you have done to us? One of the people might easily have lain with your wife, and you would have brought guilt upon us.”
verses.after: “What have you done to us?” Abimelech said. “Someone here could easily have slept with your wife. You would have brought guilt on us!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Abimelech said, “What is this you have done to us? One of the people might easily have lain with your wife, and you would have brought guilt upon us.”

verses.rationale: Keep touches as the broad threat-triggering verb and preserve the force of the doubled death construction.
verses.before: So Abimelech warned all the people, saying, “Whoever touches this man or his wife will surely be put to death.”
verses.after: Abimelech ordered all the people, “Anyone who touches this man or his wife must be put to death.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So Abimelech warned all the people, saying, “Whoever touches this man or his wife shall surely be put to death.”

verses.rationale: Retain the explicit hundredfold yield and connect blessing to the following account of growing wealth.
verses.before: Isaac sowed in that land and reaped in the same year a hundredfold. And the LORD blessed him.
verses.after: Isaac sowed crops in that land and harvested a hundredfold that same year. The LORD blessed him,
verses.tsw_comparator: Isaac sowed in that land and reaped in the same year a hundredfold. And the LORD blessed him.

verses.rationale: Reproduce the repeated g-d-l progression with grew and grew rather than losing its cumulative rhythm.
verses.before: The man became rich and continued to prosper until he became very wealthy.
verses.after: and his wealth grew and grew until he was very rich.
verses.tsw_comparator: The man became rich and continued to prosper until he became very wealthy.

verses.rationale: Take avuddah rabbah as a large serving household in the property context; note the alternative emphasis on extensive work or holdings.
verses.before: He had possessions of flocks and herds and many servants, so that the Philistines envied him.
verses.after: He owned flocks and herds and had a large household of servants. The Philistines envied him.
verses.tsw_comparator: He had possessions of flocks and herds and many servants, so that the Philistines envied him.

verses.rationale: Make the background action audible while keeping the repeated father/Abraham identification and the physical filling of wells.
verses.before: Now all the wells that his father’s servants had dug in the days of Abraham his father, the Philistines stopped up, filling them with earth.
verses.after: The Philistines had stopped up all the wells his father’s servants had dug in the days of his father Abraham, filling them with earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now all the wells that his father’s servants had dug in the days of Abraham his father, the Philistines stopped up, filling them with earth.

verses.rationale: Render the comparative strength clause as an expulsion demand without reducing it to personal dislike.
verses.before: Then Abimelech said to Isaac, “Go away from us, for you have become much mightier than we.”
verses.after: Abimelech told Isaac, “Leave us. You have become far too powerful for us.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Abimelech said to Isaac, “Go away from us, for you have become much mightier than we.”

verses.rationale: Preserve departure, camping, and residence as separate actions; retain valley rather than inventing a permanent river.
verses.before: So Isaac departed from there and camped in the Valley of Gerar and settled there.
verses.after: Isaac left and camped in the valley of Gerar. He made his home there.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Isaac departed from there and camped in the Valley of Gerar and settled there.

verses.rationale: Keep both the chronology after Abraham’s death and the deliberate restoration of the old names.
verses.before: Isaac dug again the wells of water that had been dug in the days of Abraham his father, which the Philistines had stopped up after the death of Abraham. And he gave them the names that his father had given them.
verses.after: He reopened the wells dug in the days of his father Abraham, which the Philistines had stopped up after Abraham’s death. He gave the wells the same names his father had given them.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Isaac dug again the wells of water that had been dug in the days of Abraham his father, which the Philistines had stopped up after the death of Abraham. And he gave them the names that his father had given them.

verses.rationale: Render living water as flowing water in a well context, with the literal expression preserved in vocabulary.
verses.before: But when Isaac’s servants dug in the valley, they found there a well of spring water.
verses.after: Isaac’s servants dug in the valley and found a well of fresh, flowing water.
verses.tsw_comparator: But when Isaac’s servants dug in the valley, they found there a well of spring water.

verses.rationale: Identify Isaac as the naming subject and retain the ownership dispute that explains Esek.
verses.before: The herdsmen of Gerar quarreled with Isaac’s herdsmen, saying, “The water is ours.” So he called the name of the well Esek, because they contended with him.
verses.after: The herders of Gerar argued with Isaac’s herders. “The water belongs to us!” they said. Isaac named the well Esek because they disputed it with him.
verses.tsw_comparator: The herdsmen of Gerar quarreled with Isaac’s herdsmen, saying, “The water is ours.” So he called the name of the well Esek, because they contended with him.

verses.rationale: Preserve the repeated conflict and second name without adding speakers absent from this verse.
verses.before: Then they dug another well, and they quarreled over that one also. So he called its name Sitnah.
verses.after: They dug another well, but there was an argument over that one too. Isaac named it Sitnah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then they dug another well, and they quarreled over that one also. So he called its name Sitnah.

verses.rationale: Retain room and fruitfulness as the spoken explanation of Rehoboth, rather than substituting general success.
verses.before: And he moved on from there and dug another well, and over it they did not quarrel. So he called its name Rehoboth, saying, “For now the LORD has made room for us, and we will be fruitful in the land.”
verses.after: He moved on and dug another well, and no one argued over it. He named it Rehoboth, saying, “Now the LORD has made room for us, and we will be fruitful in the land.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And he moved on from there and dug another well, and over it they did not quarrel. So he called its name Rehoboth, saying, “For now the LORD has made room for us, and we shall be fruitful in the land.”

verses.rationale: Retain this clear short journey sentence; the ascent and place name need no change for distinctness.
verses.before: From there he went up to Beersheba.
verses.after: From there he went up to Beersheba.
verses.tsw_comparator: From there he went up to Beersheba.

verses.rationale: Keep the appearance, reassurance, presence, blessing, descendants, and Abraham rationale in manageable spoken units.
verses.before: And the LORD appeared to him that same night and said, “I am the God of Abraham your father. Do not fear, for I am with you and will bless you and multiply your offspring for the sake of Abraham my servant.”
verses.after: That night the LORD appeared to him and said, “I am the God of your father Abraham. Do not be afraid, for I am with you. I will bless you and multiply your descendants for the sake of my servant Abraham.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD appeared to him that same night and said, “I am the God of Abraham your father. Do not fear, for I am with you and will bless you and multiply your offspring for the sake of Abraham my servant.”

verses.rationale: Identify Isaac and retain the repeated there that gathers worship, dwelling, and digging into one location.
verses.before: So he built an altar there and called upon the name of the LORD and pitched his tent there. And there Isaac’s servants dug a well.
verses.after: Isaac built an altar there and called on the name of the LORD. He pitched his tent there, and his servants dug a well.
verses.tsw_comparator: So he built an altar there and called upon the name of the LORD and pitched his tent there. And there Isaac’s servants dug a well.

verses.rationale: Retain the named diplomatic companions; render merea as adviser in a royal setting, noting friend as the literal relational term.
verses.before: Then Abimelech came to him from Gerar with Ahuzzath his adviser and Phicol the commander of his army.
verses.after: Abimelech came to him from Gerar with Ahuzzath, his adviser, and Phicol, the commander of his army.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Abimelech came to him from Gerar with Ahuzzath his adviser and Phicol the commander of his army.

verses.rationale: Preserve hated rather than softening the accusation, with the question separated for oral clarity.
verses.before: Isaac said to them, “Why have you come to me, seeing that you hate me and have sent me away from you?”
verses.after: Isaac asked them, “Why have you come to me? You hated me and drove me away.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Isaac said to them, “Why have you come to me, seeing that you hate me and have sent me away from you?”

verses.rationale: Retain emphatic seeing and both oath and covenant; recast the repeated between-us wording while keeping its emphatic naming of both parties.
verses.before: They said, “We clearly see that the LORD has been with you. So we said, ‘Let there now be an oath between us, between us and you, and let us make a covenant with you,
verses.after: They answered, “We have seen clearly that the LORD has been with you. So we said, ‘Let an oath bind us, you and us.’ Let us make a covenant with you:
verses.tsw_comparator: They said, “We clearly see that the LORD has been with you. So we said, ‘Let there now be an oath between us, between us and you, and let us make a covenant with you,

verses.rationale: Keep the visitors’ claim of harmless treatment as their speech, not the narrator’s verdict, and retain peace against Isaac’s expulsion charge.
verses.before: that you will do us no harm, just as we have not touched you and have done nothing to you but good and have sent you away in peace. You are now blessed by the LORD.’”
verses.after: you must do us no harm, just as we did not touch you. We did you only good and sent you away in peace. Now you are blessed by the LORD.”
verses.tsw_comparator: that you will do us no harm, just as we have not touched you and have done nothing to you but good and have sent you away in peace. You are now blessed by the LORD.’”

verses.rationale: Identify the host and retain the shared eating and drinking that accompany the covenant.
verses.before: So he made them a feast, and they ate and drank.
verses.after: Isaac prepared a feast for them, and they ate and drank.
verses.tsw_comparator: So he made them a feast, and they ate and drank.

verses.rationale: Render reciprocal oath-taking clearly and retain the second departure-in-peace phrase.
verses.before: In the morning they rose early and exchanged oaths. Then Isaac sent them on their way, and they departed from him in peace.
verses.after: Early the next morning they swore an oath to one another. Isaac sent them on their way, and they left him in peace.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the morning they rose early and exchanged oaths. Then Isaac sent them on their way, and they departed from him in peace.

verses.rationale: Keep the discovery’s timing and the servants’ own announcement without merging it into the narrator’s summary.
verses.before: That same day Isaac’s servants came and told him about the well they had dug and said to him, “We have found water.”
verses.after: That same day Isaac’s servants came and told him about the well they had dug. “We have found water!” they said.
verses.tsw_comparator: That same day Isaac’s servants came and told him about the well they had dug and said to him, “We have found water.”

verses.rationale: Keep the Hebrew well name rather than flattening its seven/oath associations; do not harmonize away the naming account in chapter 21.
verses.before: He called it Shibah. Therefore the name of the city is Beersheba to this day.
verses.after: He named it Shibah. That is why the city is called Beersheba to this day.
verses.tsw_comparator: He called it Shibah. Therefore the name of the city is Beersheba to this day.

verses.rationale: Preserve age, both wives, both fathers, and both Hittite identifiers; do not harmonize later differing wife names.
verses.before: When Esau was forty years old, he took Judith the daughter of Beeri the Hittite as wife, and Basemath the daughter of Elon the Hittite.
verses.after: When Esau was forty years old, he married Judith, daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Basemath, daughter of Elon the Hittite.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Esau was forty years old, he took Judith the daughter of Beeri the Hittite as wife, and Basemath the daughter of Elon the Hittite.

verses.rationale: Retain the bitter-spirit idiom as relational distress without supplying motives or making the narrator condemn an ethnicity.
verses.before: And they made life bitter for Isaac and Rebekah.
verses.after: They brought bitterness to Isaac and Rebekah.
verses.tsw_comparator: And they made life bitter for Isaac and Rebekah.

verses.rationale: Keep the blindness that governs the scene and identify the answering son for listeners.
verses.before: When Isaac was old and his eyes were dim so that he could not see, he called Esau his older son and said to him, “My son.” And he answered, “Here I am.”
verses.after: Isaac had grown old, and his eyes were too dim to see. He called his older son Esau. “My son!” he said. “Here I am,” Esau answered.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Isaac was old and his eyes were dim so that he could not see, he called Esau his older son and said to him, “My son.” And he answered, “Here I am.”

verses.rationale: Render day of my death idiomatically without claiming that death is objectively imminent.
verses.before: He said, “See now, I am old. I do not know the day of my death.
verses.after: Isaac said, “I am old now, and I do not know when I will die.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “See now, I am old. I do not know the day of my death.

verses.rationale: Choose quiver for rare teli and game according to the recorded qere tsayid; retain the ketiv and qere in the source binding.
verses.before: Now then, take your weapons, your quiver and your bow, and go out into the field and hunt game for me.
verses.after: Take your hunting gear—your quiver and bow—and go out into the country. Hunt some game for me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now then, take your weapons, your quiver and your bow, and go out into the field and hunt game for me.

verses.rationale: Render nafshi as wholehearted personal blessing rather than a separable soul; keep meal, purpose, and death sequence.
verses.before: Prepare for me the delicious food that I love and bring it to me, so that I may eat, that my soul may bless you before I die.”
verses.after: Make me a meal I enjoy and bring it to me to eat, so that I may give you my heartfelt blessing before I die.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Prepare for me the delicious food that I love and bring it to me, so that I may eat, that my soul may bless you before I die.”

verses.rationale: Keep Rebekah’s ongoing listening and let the temporal sentence continue into verse 6.
verses.before: Now Rebekah was listening when Isaac spoke to Esau his son. So when Esau went to the field to hunt game and bring it,
verses.after: Rebekah was listening as Isaac spoke to his son Esau. When Esau went out into the country to hunt game and bring it back,
verses.tsw_comparator: Now Rebekah was listening when Isaac spoke to Esau his son. So when Esau went to the field to hunt game and bring it,

verses.rationale: Preserve her son versus his son and the familial relationships in Rebekah’s report.
verses.before: Rebekah said to Jacob her son, “See, I heard your father speak to Esau your brother, saying,
verses.after: she said to her son Jacob, “I heard your father tell your brother Esau,
verses.tsw_comparator: Rebekah said to Jacob her son, “See, I heard your father speak to Esau your brother, saying,

verses.rationale: Retain Rebekah’s added in-the-LORD’s-presence phrase without inserting it retroactively into Isaac’s original speech.
verses.before: ‘Bring me game and prepare delicious food for me, that I may eat and bless you before the LORD before my death.’
verses.after: ‘Bring me game and make me a meal I enjoy. I will eat it and bless you in the LORD’s presence before I die.’
verses.tsw_comparator: ‘Bring me game and prepare delicious food for me, that I may eat and bless you before the LORD before my death.’

verses.rationale: Render listen-to-my-voice as obedient listening and retain the command function rather than generic advice.
verses.before: Now therefore, my son, listen to my voice as I command you.
verses.after: Now, my son, listen to me and do what I tell you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now therefore, my son, listen to my voice as I command you.

verses.rationale: Preserve the two kids and Rebekah’s own preparation; avoid amplifying good into an unsupported superlative.
verses.before: Go now to the flock and bring me two choice young goats, so that I may prepare from them delicious food for your father, such as he loves.
verses.after: Go to the flock and get me two good young goats. I will make them into a meal your father enjoys.
verses.tsw_comparator: Go now to the flock and bring me two choice young goats, so that I may prepare from them delicious food for your father, such as he loves.

verses.rationale: Keep Jacob’s assigned action and its stated purpose, not an added narrator endorsement.
verses.before: Then you will bring it to your father to eat, so that he may bless you before his death.”
verses.after: Take it to your father to eat, so that he will bless you before he dies.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then you shall bring it to your father to eat, so that he may bless you before his death.”

verses.rationale: Make the tactile contrast idiomatic and keep its relevance to Isaac’s inability to see.
verses.before: Yet Jacob said to Rebekah his mother, “See, Esau my brother is a hairy man, and I am a smooth man.
verses.after: Jacob said to his mother Rebekah, “But my brother Esau is hairy, and my skin is smooth.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Jacob said to Rebekah his mother, “See, Esau my brother is a hairy man, and I am a smooth man.

verses.rationale: Choose the mocking sense of metatea and retain Jacob’s fear of discovery rather than adding moral remorse.
verses.before: Perhaps my father will feel me, and I will seem to him to be mocking him and bring a curse upon myself and not a blessing.”
verses.after: What if my father feels me? He will think I am making a fool of him. I will bring a curse on myself instead of a blessing.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Perhaps my father will feel me, and I shall seem to him to be mocking him and bring a curse upon myself and not a blessing.”

verses.rationale: Preserve Rebekah’s acceptance of the curse and her repeated demand for compliance.
verses.before: His mother said to him, “Let your curse be upon me, my son. Only obey my voice, and go, bring them to me.”
verses.after: His mother answered, “Let the curse fall on me, my son. Just listen to me. Go and get them.”
verses.tsw_comparator: His mother said to him, “Let your curse be upon me, my son. Only obey my voice, and go, bring them to me.”

verses.rationale: Name Jacob at the scene transition and specify the goats as the antecedent of them.
verses.before: So he went and took them and brought them to his mother, and his mother prepared delicious food such as his father loved.
verses.after: Jacob went and got the goats and brought them to his mother. She made a meal his father enjoyed.
verses.tsw_comparator: So he went and took them and brought them to his mother, and his mother prepared delicious food such as his father loved.

verses.rationale: Keep older and younger juxtaposed and preserve the desirable clothes kept with Rebekah.
verses.before: Then Rebekah took the best garments of Esau her older son, which were with her in the house, and put them on Jacob her younger son.
verses.after: Rebekah took the fine clothes of her older son Esau, which she kept in the house, and dressed her younger son Jacob in them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Rebekah took the best garments of Esau her older son, which were with her in the house, and put them on Jacob her younger son.

verses.rationale: Retain both covered body parts and the goatskins without inventing gloves or a fastening method.
verses.before: And the skins of the young goats she put on his hands and on the smooth part of his neck.
verses.after: She covered his hands and the smooth part of his neck with the young goats’ skins.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the skins of the young goats she put on his hands and on the smooth part of his neck.

verses.rationale: Render gave-into-the-hand as handed, retaining bread as distinct from the prepared meal and naming its recipient.
verses.before: Then she gave the delicious food and the bread that she had prepared into the hand of Jacob her son.
verses.after: Then she handed her son Jacob the meal and the bread she had made.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then she gave the delicious food and the bread that she had prepared into the hand of Jacob her son.

verses.rationale: Make each voice explicit while preserving Isaac’s inability to identify the visitor.
verses.before: So he went in to his father and said, “My father.” And he said, “Here I am. Who are you, my son?”
verses.after: Jacob went to his father and said, “My father!” “Here I am,” Isaac answered. “Who are you, my son?”
verses.tsw_comparator: So he went in to his father and said, “My father.” And he said, “Here I am. Who are you, my son?”

verses.rationale: Keep the direct false identification and firstborn claim; render the repeated nefesh idiom consistently with verse 4.
verses.before: Jacob said to his father, “I am Esau your firstborn. I have done as you told me. Rise now, sit and eat of my game, so that your soul may bless me.”
verses.after: “I am Esau, your firstborn,” Jacob told his father. “I have done what you asked. Please sit up and eat some of my game, so that you may give me your heartfelt blessing.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Jacob said to his father, “I am Esau your firstborn. I have done as you told me. Rise now, sit and eat of my game, so that your soul may bless me.”

verses.rationale: Keep the encounter idiom in hiqrah rather than generalizing to success, and preserve your God in Jacob’s reply.
verses.before: Yet Isaac said to his son, “How is it that you have found it so quickly, my son?” He answered, “Because the LORD your God granted me success.”
verses.after: Isaac asked his son, “How did you find it so quickly, my son?” Jacob answered, “The LORD your God brought it into my path.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But Isaac said to his son, “How is it that you have found it so quickly, my son?” He answered, “Because the LORD your God granted me success.”

verses.rationale: Separate the tactile request from the repeated identity question without eliminating the uncertainty.
verses.before: Then Isaac said to Jacob, “Come near, that I may feel you, my son, to know whether you are really my son Esau or not.”
verses.after: Isaac said to Jacob, “Come closer, my son, and let me feel you. Are you really my son Esau or not?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Isaac said to Jacob, “Come near, that I may feel you, my son, to know whether you are really my son Esau or not.”

verses.rationale: Retain the balanced repeated voice/hands wording that carries Isaac’s divided perception.
verses.before: So Jacob went near to Isaac his father, who felt him and said, “The voice is Jacob’s voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau.”
verses.after: Jacob went close to his father Isaac, who felt him and said, “The voice is Jacob’s voice, but the hands are Esau’s hands.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So Jacob went near to Isaac his father, who felt him and said, “The voice is Jacob’s voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau.”

verses.rationale: Name Jacob and Isaac to keep the causal statement and blessing referents clear; leave the blessing summary in its source position.
verses.before: And he did not recognize him, because his hands were hairy like his brother Esau’s hands. So he blessed him.
verses.after: He did not recognize Jacob, because his hands were hairy like his brother Esau’s. So Isaac blessed him.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he did not recognize him, because his hands were hairy like his brother Esau’s hands. So he blessed him.

verses.rationale: Retain the repeated question and bare affirmative instead of compressing a deliberately prolonged deception.
verses.before: He said, “Are you really my son Esau?” He answered, “I am.”
verses.after: “Are you really my son Esau?” Isaac asked. “I am,” Jacob answered.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “Are you really my son Esau?” He answered, “I am.”

verses.rationale: Restore the explicit nefesh idiom omitted from the prior English here; name the servers and eater without changing the actions.
verses.before: Then he said, “Bring it near to me, that I may eat of my son’s game and bless you.” So he brought it near to him, and he ate. And he brought him wine, and he drank.
verses.after: Isaac said, “Bring it here so I can eat my son’s game and give you my heartfelt blessing.” Jacob brought it, and Isaac ate. Then Jacob brought him wine, and he drank.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he said, “Bring it near to me, that I may eat of my son’s game and bless you.” So he brought it near to him, and he ate. And he brought him wine, and he drank.

verses.rationale: Retain the father-son address and the next sense-test as a direct request.
verses.before: Then his father Isaac said to him, “Come near and kiss me, my son.”
verses.after: Then his father Isaac said, “Come closer and kiss me, my son.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then his father Isaac said to him, “Come near and kiss me, my son.”

verses.rationale: Keep smelling before blessing and the repeated scent/field image; begin poetry inside the verse paragraph.
verses.before: So he came near and kissed him. And he smelled the smell of his garments and blessed him and said, “See, the smell of my son is as the smell of a field that the LORD has blessed.
verses.after: Jacob came close and kissed him. Isaac smelled his clothes and blessed him: “Ah, my son’s scent is like the scent of a field the LORD has blessed.
verses.tsw_comparator: So he came near and kissed him. And he smelled the smell of his garments and blessed him and said, “See, the smell of my son is as the smell of a field that the LORD has blessed.

verses.rationale: Retain dew, fatness rendered richness, grain, and tirosh as new wine in three parallel lines.
verses.before: May God give you of the dew of heaven and of the richness of the earth, and abundance of grain and wine.
verses.after: May God give you dew from the heavens, the richness of the earth, and abundant grain and new wine.
verses.tsw_comparator: May God give you of the dew of heaven and of the richness of the earth, and abundance of grain and wine.

verses.rationale: Preserve gendered brothers/mother’s sons, the command be lord, and the curse/blessing pair; follow the recorded bowing qere.
verses.before: Let peoples serve you, and nations bow down to you. Be lord over your brothers, and may your mother’s sons bow down to you. Cursed be everyone who curses you, and blessed be everyone who blesses you.”
verses.after: May peoples serve you and nations bow before you. Be lord over your brothers; may your mother’s sons bow before you. Cursed be those who curse you, and blessed be those who bless you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Let peoples serve you, and nations bow down to you. Be lord over your brothers, and may your mother’s sons bow down to you. Cursed be everyone who curses you, and blessed be everyone who blesses you.”

verses.rationale: Render the emphatic immediate departure without the prior nested temporal clause; retain the nearly overlapping arrivals.
verses.before: As soon as Isaac had finished blessing Jacob, when Jacob had scarcely gone out from the presence of Isaac his father, Esau his brother came in from his hunting.
verses.after: Isaac finished blessing Jacob. Jacob had barely left his father Isaac when his brother Esau came back from hunting.
verses.tsw_comparator: As soon as Isaac had finished blessing Jacob, when Jacob had scarcely gone out from the presence of Isaac his father, Esau his brother came in from his hunting.

verses.rationale: Keep Esau’s echo of the requested meal and nefesh blessing, using polite direct address for the third-person courtesy form.
verses.before: He also prepared delicious food and brought it to his father. And he said to his father, “Let my father arise and eat of his son’s game, so that your soul may bless me.”
verses.after: Esau too made a meal his father enjoyed and brought it to him. “Please sit up, my father, and eat some of your son’s game,” he said, “so that you may give me your heartfelt blessing.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He also prepared delicious food and brought it to his father. And he said to his father, “Let my father arise and eat of his son’s game, so that your soul may bless me.”

verses.rationale: Keep the delayed name and the firstborn emphasis as the disclosure that triggers Isaac’s reaction.
verses.before: Isaac his father said to him, “Who are you?” He answered, “I am your son, your firstborn, Esau.”
verses.after: His father Isaac asked, “Who are you?” “I am your son,” he answered, “your firstborn, Esau.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Isaac his father said to him, “Who are you?” He answered, “I am your son, your firstborn, Esau.”

verses.rationale: Retain the intense trembling and emphatic lasting blessing; render mikkol as some of everything, not necessarily consuming every scrap.
verses.before: Then Isaac trembled with exceedingly great trembling and said, “Who then was it that hunted game and brought it to me? I ate it all before you came, and I blessed him—and indeed he will be blessed.”
verses.after: Isaac began trembling violently. “Who was it, then, who hunted game and brought it to me?” he asked. “I ate some of everything before you arrived, and I blessed him. And blessed he will remain!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Isaac trembled with exceedingly great trembling and said, “Who then was it that hunted game and brought it to me? I ate it all before you came, and I blessed him—and indeed he shall be blessed.”

verses.rationale: Keep Esau’s audible grief and personal appeal without a judgment on his entitlement or character.
verses.before: When Esau heard the words of his father, he cried out with an exceedingly great and bitter cry and said to his father, “Bless me, even me also, my father!”
verses.after: When Esau heard his father’s words, he let out a loud, bitter cry. “Bless me too, my father!” he pleaded.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Esau heard the words of his father, he cried out with an exceedingly great and bitter cry and said to his father, “Bless me, even me also, my father!”

verses.rationale: Keep deceit explicit and identify Isaac as the speaker rather than softening the taking.
verses.before: But he said, “Your brother came deceitfully, and he has taken away your blessing.”
verses.after: Isaac said, “Your brother came with deceit and took your blessing.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But he said, “Your brother came deceitfully, and he has taken away your blessing.”

verses.rationale: Choose pushed me aside for the supplanting wordplay; keep birthright and blessing distinct and the allegation in Esau’s voice.
verses.before: Esau said, “Is he not rightly named Jacob? For he has supplanted me these two times. He took away my birthright, and now he has taken away my blessing.” Then he said, “Have you not reserved a blessing for me?”
verses.after: Esau said, “Wasn’t he rightly named Jacob? Twice now he has pushed me aside. He took my birthright, and now he has taken my blessing!” Then he asked, “Haven’t you kept a blessing for me?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Esau said, “Is he not rightly named Jacob? For he has supplanted me these two times. He took away my birthright, and now he has taken away my blessing.” Then he said, “Have you not reserved a blessing for me?”

verses.rationale: Retain the force of lord and servants and both agricultural provisions; do not turn the claim into mere future advice.
verses.before: Isaac answered and said to Esau, “Look, I have made him lord over you, and all his brothers I have given to him as servants, and with grain and wine I have sustained him. What then can I do for you, my son?”
verses.after: Isaac answered Esau, “I have made him lord over you and given him all his brothers as servants. I have provided him with grain and new wine. What can I do for you now, my son?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Isaac answered and said to Esau, “Behold, I have made him lord over you, and all his brothers I have given to him as servants, and with grain and wine I have sustained him. What then can I do for you, my son?”

verses.rationale: Keep both my-father appeals and the distinct weeping following the earlier cry.
verses.before: Esau said to his father, “Have you but one blessing, my father? Bless me, even me also, my father.” And Esau lifted up his voice and wept.
verses.after: “Do you have only one blessing, my father?” Esau asked. “Bless me too, my father!” And Esau wept aloud.
verses.tsw_comparator: Esau said to his father, “Have you but one blessing, my father? Bless me, even me also, my father.” And Esau lifted up his voice and wept.

verses.rationale: Retain the separative reading of min provisionally; disclose the consequential alternative in/of the earth’s richness in Notes.
verses.before: Then Isaac his father answered and said to him, “Look, away from the richness of the earth will your dwelling be, and away from the dew of heaven above.
verses.after: His father Isaac answered: “Your home will be away from the richness of the earth, away from the dew of the heavens above.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Isaac his father answered and said to him, “Behold, away from the richness of the earth shall your dwelling be, and away from the dew of heaven above.

verses.rationale: Keep sword, service, and the concrete yoke; retain restless for difficult tarid without claiming a settled historical fulfillment.
verses.before: By your sword you will live, and you will serve your brother. But when you grow restless, you will break his yoke from your neck.”
verses.after: You will live by your sword and serve your brother. But when you grow restless, you will tear his yoke from your neck.”
verses.tsw_comparator: By your sword you shall live, and you shall serve your brother. But when you grow restless, you shall break his yoke from your neck.”

verses.rationale: Keep persistent hostility and the murder intention; leave the expectation of Isaac’s death as Esau’s thought.
verses.before: Now Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing with which his father had blessed him. And Esau said in his heart, “The days of mourning for my father are approaching; then I will kill my brother Jacob.”
verses.after: Esau bore a grudge against Jacob because of the blessing his father had given him. He said to himself, “The days of mourning for my father are near. Then I will kill my brother Jacob.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Now Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing with which his father had blessed him. And Esau said in his heart, “The days of mourning for my father are approaching; then I will kill my brother Jacob.”

verses.rationale: Keep the source’s disturbing comforting-himself expression and the unspecified report to Rebekah without inventing an informer.
verses.before: But the words of Esau her older son were told to Rebekah. So she sent and called Jacob her younger son and said to him, “See, your brother Esau comforts himself concerning you by planning to kill you.
verses.after: Rebekah was told what her older son Esau had said. She sent for her younger son Jacob and told him, “Your brother Esau is comforting himself with the thought of killing you.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the words of Esau her older son were told to Rebekah. So she sent and called Jacob her younger son and said to him, “See, your brother Esau comforts himself concerning you by planning to kill you.

verses.rationale: Preserve the repeated listening command, urgency, flight, kinship, and destination.
verses.before: Now therefore, my son, obey my voice. Rise and flee to Laban my brother in Haran,
verses.after: Now, my son, listen to me. Leave at once and flee to my brother Laban in Haran.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now therefore, my son, obey my voice. Rise and flee to Laban my brother in Haran,

verses.rationale: Retain the specific few-days expectation and carry the repeated until structure into verse 45 without harmonizing the eventual delay.
verses.before: and stay with him a while, until your brother’s fury turns away,
verses.after: Stay with him a few days, until your brother’s fury dies down,
verses.tsw_comparator: and stay with him a while, until your brother’s fury turns away,

verses.rationale: Preserve the repeated anger clause and Rebekah’s double-loss fear without deciding how the second loss would occur.
verses.before: until your brother’s anger turns away from you and he forgets what you have done to him. Then I will send and bring you back from there. Why should I be bereaved of both of you in one day?”
verses.after: until his anger toward you subsides and he forgets what you have done to him. Then I will send for you and bring you back. Why should I lose both of you in one day?”
verses.tsw_comparator: until your brother’s anger turns away from you and he forgets what you have done to him. Then I will send and bring you back from there. Why should I be bereaved of both of you in one day?”

verses.rationale: Retain the force of qats and the closing life-question as Rebekah’s speech; avoid a diagnosis or an invented marriage motive.
verses.before: Then Rebekah said to Isaac, “I am weary of my life because of the Hittite women. If Jacob takes a wife from the Hittite women like these, from the women of the land, what good will my life be to me?”
verses.after: Rebekah said to Isaac, “I am sick of my life because of these Hittite women. If Jacob marries a Hittite woman like these women of the land, what would I have to live for?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Rebekah said to Isaac, “I am weary of my life because of the Hittite women. If Jacob takes a wife from the Hittite women like these, from the women of the land, what good will my life be to me?”

verses.rationale: Render the prohibition as a command, retaining blessing before instruction without conflating it with the earlier deception.
verses.before: Then Isaac called Jacob and blessed him and directed him, “You will not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan.
verses.after: Isaac called Jacob, blessed him, and gave him this command: “Do not marry a Canaanite woman.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Isaac called Jacob and blessed him and directed him, “You shall not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan.

verses.rationale: Keep both maternal relationships explicit and distinguish the destination household from the permitted spouses.
verses.before: Arise, go to Paddan-aram, to the house of Bethuel your mother’s father, and take as your wife from there one of the daughters of Laban your mother’s brother.
verses.after: Go at once to Paddan-aram, to the household of your mother’s father Bethuel. Marry one of the daughters of your mother’s brother Laban.
verses.tsw_comparator: Arise, go to Paddan-aram, to the house of Bethuel your mother’s father, and take as your wife from there one of the daughters of Laban your mother’s brother.

verses.rationale: Use the established El Shaddai rendering with its uncertainty noted; keep fruitful, multiply, and assembly as linked covenant vocabulary, with becoming as the result rather than an endpoint.
verses.before: God Almighty bless you and make you fruitful and multiply you, that you may become a company of peoples.
verses.after: May God Almighty bless you, make you fruitful, and multiply you, so that you become an assembly of peoples.
verses.tsw_comparator: God Almighty bless you and make you fruitful and multiply you, that you may become a company of peoples.

verses.rationale: Retain the blessing’s Abraham link, descendants with Jacob, possession, and present stranger status.
verses.before: May he give the blessing of Abraham to you and to your offspring with you, that you may take possession of the land of your sojournings that God gave to Abraham.”
verses.after: May he give Abraham’s blessing to you and your descendants with you, so that you may possess the land where you live as a stranger, the land God gave Abraham.”
verses.tsw_comparator: May he give the blessing of Abraham to you and to your offspring with you, that you may take possession of the land of your sojournings that God gave to Abraham.”

verses.rationale: Break the long kinship chain into two sentences without dropping Bethuel’s identification or either son.
verses.before: Thus Isaac sent Jacob away. And he went to Paddan-aram, to Laban, the son of Bethuel the Aramean, the brother of Rebekah, Jacob’s and Esau’s mother.
verses.after: Isaac sent Jacob away, and he went to Paddan-aram, to Laban son of Bethuel the Aramean. Laban was the brother of Rebekah, the mother of Jacob and Esau.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus Isaac sent Jacob away. And he went to Paddan-aram, to Laban, the son of Bethuel the Aramean, the brother of Rebekah, Jacob’s and Esau’s mother.

verses.rationale: Make the reported command comprehensible while keeping Esau’s perception, the blessing, and marriage purpose; do not add an act of overhearing.
verses.before: Now Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob and sent him away to Paddan-aram to take a wife from there, and that as he blessed him he directed him, “You will not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan,”
verses.after: Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob and sent him to Paddan-aram to marry a woman from there. In blessing him, Isaac had commanded, “Do not marry a Canaanite woman.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Now Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob and sent him away to Paddan-aram to take a wife from there, and that as he blessed him he directed him, “You shall not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan,”

verses.rationale: Retain obedience to both parents as its own sentence within the report of Esau’s observations.
verses.before: and that Jacob had obeyed his father and his mother and gone to Paddan-aram.
verses.after: Jacob had listened to his father and mother and gone to Paddan-aram.
verses.tsw_comparator: and that Jacob had obeyed his father and his mother and gone to Paddan-aram.

verses.rationale: Render evil-in-his-eyes as Isaac’s disapproval, not an objective moral judgment on the women.
verses.before: So when Esau saw that the daughters of Canaan did not please Isaac his father,
verses.after: Esau understood that his father Isaac disapproved of Canaanite women.
verses.tsw_comparator: So when Esau saw that the daughters of Canaan did not please Isaac his father,

verses.rationale: Preserve all named relationships and the additional marriage without harmonizing Mahalath with later wife lists.
verses.before: Esau went to Ishmael and took as his wife, besides the wives he had, Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael, Abraham’s son, the sister of Nebaioth.
verses.after: So he went to Ishmael and married Mahalath, daughter of Abraham’s son Ishmael and sister of Nebaioth, in addition to the wives he already had.
verses.tsw_comparator: Esau went to Ishmael and took as his wife, besides the wives he had, Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael, Abraham’s son, the sister of Nebaioth.

verses.rationale: Keep the departure and destination without implying he had already arrived.
verses.before: Jacob left Beersheba and went toward Haran.
verses.after: Jacob left Beersheba and set out for Haran.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jacob left Beersheba and went toward Haran.

verses.rationale: Render meraashot as by his head rather than asserting a stone pillow; singular stone follows the resumptive verse 18.
verses.before: And he came to a certain place and stayed there that night, because the sun had set. Taking one of the stones of the place, he put it under his head and lay down in that place to sleep.
verses.after: He came to a place and spent the night there because the sun had set. He took one of the stones there, placed it by his head, and lay down to sleep in that place.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he came to a certain place and stayed there that night, because the sun had set. Taking one of the stones of the place, he put it under his head and lay down in that place to sleep.

verses.rationale: Retain the two behold presentations, ascending before descending, and stairway as a provisional rendering of the rare sullam; no architectural reconstruction is asserted.
verses.before: And he dreamed, and look, there was a stairway set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven. And look, the angels of God were ascending and descending on it.
verses.after: He dreamed: there was a stairway standing on the earth, its top reaching the heavens. And there were God’s messengers, going up and coming down on it.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he dreamed, and behold, there was a stairway set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven. And behold, the angels of God were ascending and descending on it.

verses.rationale: Choose above-it for alav while noting beside-Jacob as possible; render father Abraham as grandfather to clarify the actual relationship.
verses.before: And look, the LORD stood above it and said, “I am the LORD, the God of Abraham your father and the God of Isaac. The land on which you lie I will give to you and to your offspring.
verses.after: And there was the LORD, standing above it. He said, “I am the LORD, the God of your grandfather Abraham and the God of Isaac. I will give the land you are lying on to you and your descendants.
verses.tsw_comparator: And behold, the LORD stood above it and said, “I am the LORD, the God of Abraham your father and the God of Isaac. The land on which you lie I will give to you and to your offspring.

verses.rationale: Retain dust, all four directions, and the singular you representing Jacob’s line; use the earlier Niphal blessing rendering with the alternative noted.
verses.before: Your offspring will be like the dust of the earth, and you will spread abroad to the west and to the east and to the north and to the south, and in you and your offspring will all the families of the earth be blessed.
verses.after: Your descendants will be like the dust of the earth. You will spread out to the west and east, to the north and south. Through you and your descendants all the families of the earth will be blessed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your offspring shall be like the dust of the earth, and you shall spread abroad to the west and to the east and to the north and to the south, and in you and your offspring shall all the families of the earth be blessed.

verses.rationale: Keep emphatic presence, guarding, return, and until-fulfillment without implying abandonment afterward.
verses.before: Look, I am with you and will keep you wherever you go, and will bring you back to this land. For I will not leave you until I have done what I have spoken to you.”
verses.after: Look, I am with you. I will guard you wherever you go and bring you back to this land. I will not leave you until I have done what I promised you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Behold, I am with you and will keep you wherever you go, and will bring you back to this land. For I will not leave you until I have done what I have spoken to you.”

verses.rationale: Retain the contrast between divine presence and Jacob’s prior unawareness without turning it into a theory of sacred space.
verses.before: Then Jacob awoke from his sleep and said, “Surely the LORD is in this place, and I did not know it.”
verses.after: Jacob woke from sleep and said, “The LORD really is in this place, and I did not know it!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Jacob awoke from his sleep and said, “Surely the LORD is in this place, and I did not know it.”

verses.rationale: Preserve the repeated fear root rather than making awesome merely enthusiastic; keep house and gate as ancient spatial images.
verses.before: And he was afraid and said, “How awesome is this place! This is none other than the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven.”
verses.after: He was afraid. “How fearsome this place is!” he said. “This is nothing less than God’s house, the gate of the heavens!”
verses.tsw_comparator: And he was afraid and said, “How awesome is this place! This is none other than the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven.”

verses.rationale: Keep the stone’s earlier location and all three ritual actions without identifying the pillar as a building.
verses.before: So early in the morning Jacob took the stone that he had put under his head and set it up for a pillar and poured oil on the top of it.
verses.after: Early in the morning Jacob took the stone he had placed by his head and set it upright as a pillar. He poured oil over its top.
verses.tsw_comparator: So early in the morning Jacob took the stone that he had put under his head and set it up for a pillar and poured oil on the top of it.

verses.rationale: Preserve the distinction between place and city and give the name’s meaning in vocabulary.
verses.before: He called the name of that place Bethel, but the name of the city was Luz at the first.
verses.after: He named the place Bethel, though the city had formerly been called Luz.
verses.tsw_comparator: He called the name of that place Bethel, but the name of the city was Luz at the first.

verses.rationale: Keep the conditional opening and concrete bread/clothes requests; repeat if only as English coordination within one condition.
verses.before: Then Jacob made a vow, saying, “If God will be with me and will keep me in this way that I go, and will give me bread to eat and clothing to wear,
verses.after: Jacob made a vow: “If God is with me and guards me on this journey, if he gives me bread to eat and clothes to wear,
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Jacob made a vow, saying, “If God will be with me and will keep me in this way that I go, and will give me bread to eat and clothing to wear,

verses.rationale: Place the main-clause boundary at then the LORD provisionally; note that this clause may instead complete the condition.
verses.before: so that I come again to my father’s house in peace, then the LORD will be my God,
verses.after: and I return to my father’s home in peace, then the LORD will be my God.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that I come again to my father’s house in peace, then the LORD shall be my God,

verses.rationale: Preserve the emphatic tenth, the shift into direct address to God, and the startling stone/house claim without explaining it away.
verses.before: and this stone, which I have set up for a pillar, will be God’s house. And of all that you give me I will surely give a tenth to you.”
verses.after: This stone I have set up as a pillar will be God’s house. And of everything you give me, I will surely give you a tenth.”
verses.tsw_comparator: and this stone, which I have set up for a pillar, shall be God’s house. And of all that you give me I will surely give a tenth to you.”
